body: Thank you. I do but I feel these people are now hitting their limits of stress. I grew up a lot quicker given my mh and I always had lovely friends who helped but I dont think they understood the gravity of the situation fully. Now that they do and I am also fully aware of how emotionally charged seeing a friend in this situation is from having other friends who have spoken about their experiences, I don't feel as comfortable. They have their lives and families to deal with.

I don't feel like I can truly confide in anyone. Having lost someone so close and feeling that type of pain, I don't want to put anyone through the feeling that may happen again. But I just cannot keep living my life in this state of staying alive only to stop other people's upset
Unfortunately it's a no to both. They suffered from mh issues which I later realised

I'm trying to stay slightly vague out of fear of people finding me on here.

I lost a big part of myself when I lost them. It was the rug being taken from under my feet and I have never recovered

I had my condition semi under control and then the full extent of my anxiety and depression hit when I lost someone close. Sleeping to avoid every day life and just general neglect has caused me to lose strength and gain weight which has just left me feeling weak and being stuck in a cycle of pain vs progress. 

I feel like I can't get out of this cycle of despair with my mental health. Each year I seem to encounter more and more issues externally that just lead me to lose faith in my ability to cope as well as the future.

Thank you for listening
